headline: Highest risk is data leakage: aci handles CRM/email data with broad egress while plano proxies chat completions and logs/metrics, creating a plausible cross-agent exfiltration path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and act on external content via MCP/direct function calls, and plano routes OpenAI-compatible chat traffic with config files and logs. If plano forwards attacker-controlled prompts or tool outputs into aci’s workflow, aci may treat them as trusted instructions. The shared bridge is inferred from documented interfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF plano forwards untrusted model output into aci tool calls or prompts
IF aci consumes MCP/file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all plano-to-aci payloads
Require a human approval step before aci executes external instructions
Strip tool directives from plano outputs before forwarding
Disable any automatic MCP bridge between the two agents
requires-engineering: implement allowlisted command schemas

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; plano handles logs/metrics/traces and sends requests to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If either agent shares workspace or context with the other, sensitive aci data can leak through plano’s outbound inference path. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default deployments and the blast radius includes customer data.
conditions: IF aci data is placed into plano prompts, logs, or traces
IF plano forwards context containing CRM/email/calendar content to a third-party endpoint
mitigations: Keep aci and plano on separate workspaces
Redact CRM/email fields before any plano call
Disable verbose logging for shared requests
Use a local-only inference backend for plano
requires-engineering: add field-level DLP filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and aci supports multiple instances while plano does not. They can contend over shared mutable resources such as APIs, OAuth-backed services, or config files if orchestrated together. The conflict is not proven on a specific shared directory, but overlapping write-like effects and external side effects make collisions plausible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API or shared account
IF orchestration allows concurrent updates without locking
mitigations: Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Assign separate service accounts
Add optimistic concurrency checks
Pause one agent during critical updates
requires-engineering: introduce resource locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, while plano is an AI gateway that can pass model outputs onward. If plano treats aci-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or routing decisions. The interaction is inferred from documented roles rather than directly observed, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF plano forwards aci output into another model or action pipeline without verification
IF aci-generated recommendations are executed automatically
mitigations: Require schema validation on aci outputs
Insert a verification step before downstream action
Limit plano to read-only routing for aci content
Log and review high-impact actions
requires-engineering: add confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: aci processes CRM, email, calendar, and support data, which can include regulated personal data, while plano handles logs/metrics/traces and forwards chat traffic to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If the same data class flows through both, retention and residency obligations may diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a medium compliance-risk inference.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed from aci into plano logs or prompts
IF plano’s backend retention exceeds aci’s policy for the same records
mitigations: Exclude personal data from plano logs
Document retention for shared records
Route regulated data only through approved backends
Review residency settings before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention policies
